articles.title: Nevada vs New Mexico: Blanked After Halftime in a 3-31 Home Loss
articles.matchup: Final: New Mexico Lobos (8-1) 31, Nevada Wolf Pack (3-6) 3, Fri., Nov. 6, Mackay Stadium, Reno. Next: at Northern Illinois, Sat., Nov. 14, 3:30 PM ET, Huskie Stadium, DeKalb
articles.text:
Nevada Wolf Pack 3, New Mexico Lobos 31. Final score 31-3 at Mackay Stadium, and it was a long Friday night in Reno. Three and six. Two and three in the Mountain West. We hosted a ranked Lobo team and never got the second half started the way this crowd wanted.

Jacob Fernandez hit a 32-yard field goal late in the first half for our only points, cutting it to 14-3 for a minute. That was the highlight. AJ Bianco went 14 of 31 for 106 yards and lost a fumble. We rushed for minus-9 yards as a team. Six first downs. Two of 15 on third down. Ten punts from Ewan Baulch. Ninety-seven yards of offense against a New Mexico defense that sat on us for 38 minutes. Dylan LaBarbera led us with nine tackles and a sack. The effort was there. The yards were not.

Scottre Humphrey ran for 107 and two scores. Kiefer Sibley hit us for a 31-yard touchdown run. Toa Fa'avae found Cade Keith from 25 in the fourth. Nick Romero added a 37-yard field goal. They put up 374 yards and never turned it over. We turned it over once and spent the night in third-and-long. That is how you get blanked after the half on your own field.

The first half at least had a pulse when Fernandez drilled the 32-yarder. After the break it was Humphrey from 1, Keith from 25, Romero from 37, and the student section checking the exits. Hard night for a home crowd that showed up ready for a fight and got a clinic instead.

Northern Illinois on the road Saturday, Nov. 14, at 3:30 PM ET. Huskie Stadium in DeKalb. Fix the run game, win third down, and put points on the board before this season slips further. Pack up.

articles.title: New Mexico vs Nevada: Humphrey, Sibley and a 31-3 Road Statement
articles.byline: Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, The New Mexico Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: New Mexico Lobos (8-1) 31, Nevada Wolf Pack (3-6) 3, Fri., Nov. 6, Mackay Stadium, Reno. Next: vs UNLV, Sat., Nov. 14, 7:30 PM ET, University Stadium, Albuquerque
articles.text:
Thirty-one to three. Final score 31-3 at Mackay Stadium in Reno, and the Lobos just rolled into town and took the building. New Mexico 31, Nevada 3. Eight and one. Five and oh in the Mountain West. Road win number four. Keep the music on for the flight home to Albuquerque.

Scottre Humphrey ran the show on the ground. Seventeen carries for 107 yards and two scores, from 2 yards and from 1. Kiefer Sibley ripped a 31-yard touchdown run and finished with 54 yards on 12 carries. Toa Fa'avae went 14 of 20 for 150 yards and found Cade Keith from 25 in the fourth. Keith caught four for 63. Nick Romero was perfect on four extras and drilled a 37-yard field goal. We put up 374 yards of offense, 213 on the ground, and sat on the ball for 38 minutes and 36 seconds. Zero turnovers. That is Lobo football in November.

Nevada managed 97 yards and minus-9 on the ground. AJ Bianco went 14 of 31 for 106 with a fumble lost. Their only points were a 32-yard field goal from Jacob Fernandez late in the first half that made it 14-3. After that it was all turquoise. Jayden Flaker led us with six tackles. Brett Karhu had 1.5 sacks. We were 9 of 16 on third down and never let Mackay get loud for long.

First quarter: Humphrey from 2, Sibley from 31, and we were already up 14-0. Third quarter: Humphrey again from 1. Fourth: Keith from 25, then Romero from 37. Clean. Physical. Exactly the kind of road statement a ranked Mountain West leader is supposed to make on a Friday night in Reno.

UNLV comes to University Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 7:30 PM ET. Home crowd. Same grind. Same identity. Lobos up.

articles.title: Nebraska vs Illinois: Fourth Straight Loss, 13-24 in Champaign
articles.matchup: Final: Nebraska Cornhuskers (5-4) 13, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-3) 24, Fri., Nov. 6, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign. Next: at Rutgers, Sat., Nov. 14, 12:30 PM ET, SHI Stadium, Piscataway
articles.text:
Nebraska Cornhuskers 13, Illinois Fighting Illini 24. Final score 24-13 from Champaign, and it is a fourth straight loss. Five and four. Two and four in the Big Ten. We flew into Gies Memorial Stadium with a chance to snap the skid on a Friday night and left watching Illinois celebrate Dads Day.

Anthony Colandrea put up numbers. Thirty-two of 43 for 284 yards and a touchdown. Jacory Barney Jr. caught six for 93, including a 51-yard score in the fourth that cut it to 13-21 before the two-point try failed. Jamal Rule ran for 69. Mekhi Nelson opened the scoring with a 15-yard run. We outgained them in first downs, 25 to 19, and put up 426 yards to their 376. John Hohl missed both of his field goal tries. That will keep you up on the flight home.

Illinois answered every good drive we had. Katin Houser threw three touchdowns. Collin Dixon caught two of them and finished with 129 yards. Their punter, Lars Rau, ran 29 yards on a fake field goal that set up a 5-yard score to Jordan Anderson. Suddenly it was 14-7, then 21-7, then 24-13 after Ethan Moczulski's 21-yard kick. We had zero turnovers and still could not finish. Eleven penalties for 82 yards did not help. Vincent Shavers Jr. led us with seven tackles.

The fourth quarter had a pulse when Barney went long, but the two-point miss and the missed kicks earlier left us needing miracles. Illinois got the stops. We got the long flight home. Four in a row is a stretch that tests a locker room, and this one was earned the hard way on the road in Champaign.

Rutgers on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 12:30 PM ET in Piscataway. SHI Stadium. Make the kicks, clean up the flags, and get a win before Ohio State week. Go Big Red.

articles.title: Illinois vs Nebraska: Houser, Dixon, Fake Kick and a 24-13 Dads Day Win
articles.matchup: Final: Nebraska Cornhuskers (5-4) 13, Illinois Fighting Illini (6-3) 24, Fri., Nov. 6, Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign. Next: at UCLA, Fri., Nov. 13, 9:00 PM ET, Rose Bowl, Pasadena
articles.text:
Twenty-four to thirteen. Final score 24-13. Gies Memorial Stadium under the lights for Dads Day and a Hail to the Blue Out, 58,587 strong, and the Fighting Illini just ran the winning streak to four. Six and three. Four and two in the Big Ten. Champaign is loud again, and bowl talk is not a whisper anymore.

Katin Houser went 22 of 36 for 292 yards and three touchdowns. Collin Dixon was the show: eight catches for 129 yards and two scores, including a 3-yarder before the half that tied it 7-7 and a 6-yarder early in the fourth that made it 21-7. Illinois Athletics says Dixon now owns the program's single-season touchdown receptions record. Hudson Clement added five grabs for 87. And the fake field goal? Lars Rau took it 29 yards on fourth-and-12, setting up Jordan Anderson's 5-yard score for a 14-7 lead. Ethan Moczulski drilled a 21-yarder later. Perfect timing on a Friday night.

Nebraska struck first when Mekhi Nelson ran in from 15. Anthony Colandrea threw for 284 and hit Jacory Barney Jr. from 51 in the fourth to make it 13-21 after a failed two-point try. We answered with Moczulski's kick and then got stops. Matthew Bailey led us with 11 tackles. James Kreutz had 10. Zero turnovers both ways. We only ran for 84 yards as a team and still controlled the second half when it counted.

That fake kick is going straight into the Gies highlight reel. Fourth-and-12 from the Nebraska 32, and Rau just took off. Three plays later Anderson is in the end zone and the place is bouncing. Dixon's record night on top of it. Fourth straight win. Belief is back in orange and blue around Champaign.

Next stop: the Rose Bowl on Friday, Nov. 13, at 9 PM ET against UCLA. Ranked road test. Pack the same Friday night toughness we showed the Huskers. I-L-L.

articles.title: South Florida vs East Carolina: One Kick From Greenville Stings 17-20
articles.byline: Reina Valdés-Kowalski, The South Florida Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: South Florida Bulls (6-3) 17, East Carolina Pirates (5-4) 20, Fri., Nov. 6, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville. Next: vs Memphis, Thu., Nov. 12, 8:00 PM ET, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa
articles.text:
South Florida Bulls 17, East Carolina Pirates 20. Final score 20-17. A 55-yard kick at the gun in Greenville, and we walk out of Dowdy-Ficklen with a gut punch. Six and three. Two and three in the American. We had this game tied with under 10 minutes left and still flew home empty-handed after a long Friday night.

Luke Kromenhoek did his job in place of the usual starter. Seventeen of 21 for 179 yards and a touchdown, the 26-yarder to Bryson Rodgers that opened the scoring at 7-0. D.J. Crowther ran hard for 111 yards on 17 carries and added three catches for 42. Jason Collins Jr. punched in from a yard out to tie it 17-17 in the fourth. Nico Gramatica was good from 30. We put up 329 yards and never threw an interception. Zero turnovers. On paper that should travel and win you a road game in November.

Here is what killed us. One of 10 on third down. Seven punts. Emory Williams found Landon Sides twice for scores, and Sides finished with 14 catches for 126. Ashton Gray ran for 101. We led 10-3 late in the half, gave up a 15-yard Sides score before the break, then watched an 8-yarder in the third put them ahead 17-10. Grayson Howard led us with 13 tackles and half a sack. The defense kept answering until it could not answer a 55-yarder from Andrew Conrad.

Conrad's kick with two seconds left is going to live rent-free for a while. We had the ball game knotted and the clock on our side of the argument, then one swing of a leg flipped the airport mood. That is a road loss in November, not a fluke of the schedule, and it drops us in the American race.

Memphis comes to Raymond James Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8 PM ET. Home night under the lights. Fix third down, finish drives, and make Tampa loud again. Bulls up.

articles.title: East Carolina vs South Florida: Conrad's 55-Yard Stunner Wins It 20-17
articles.byline: Bartholomew 'Bart' Quidley, The East Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: South Florida Bulls (6-3) 17, East Carolina Pirates (5-4) 20, Fri., Nov. 6, Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, Greenville. Next: at Charlotte, Sat., Nov. 14, 1:00 PM ET, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte
articles.text:
Twenty to seventeen. Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium, 33,708 strong on a Friday night in Greenville, and Andrew Conrad just drilled a 55-yard field goal as time expired. East Carolina Pirates 20, South Florida Bulls 17. Final score 20-17. Five and four. Three and two in the American. One win from bowl eligibility, and the place absolutely lost its mind.

Emory Williams stepped in and delivered when we needed him most. Nineteen of 27 for 175 yards and two touchdowns, both to Landon Sides, who was everywhere: 14 catches for 126 yards, scores from 15 and 8 that flipped the half and then the third quarter. Ashton Gray ran for 101 on 18 carries and kept the chains moving. Noah Perez hit a 44-yarder in the second. We trailed 10-3 late in the half, then Williams found Sides from 15 with 31 seconds left to knot it at 10-10. Out of the break, Sides again from 8 for a 17-10 lead that felt huge in this building.

South Florida tied it at 17-17 when Jason Collins Jr. walked in from a yard out in the fourth. Luke Kromenhoek had thrown a 26-yard score to Bryson Rodgers early, and D.J. Crowther ran for 111. Our defense bent but got stops when it mattered. Kamaurri McKinley led us with 11 tackles. We turned one ball over and still found a way to finish the night.

Then the final drive. Conrad, career long, 55 yards, ball through the uprights with two seconds showing. The AP called it a lift. From the student section it looked like a rocket leaving the pad. Mitch Griffis and TJ Engleman Jr. both left earlier; Williams and Gray carried the load anyway and never flinched.

Charlotte on the road Saturday, Nov. 14, at 1 PM ET. Jerry Richardson Stadium. Take this Friday night feeling with us and punch that bowl ticket. Purple and gold forever.

articles.title: Virginia Tech vs SMU: Overton Fought, Ford Stadium Did Not Care, 51-28
articles.byline: Ruthanne Dellinger, The Virginia Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Final: Virginia Tech Hokies (6-3) 28, SMU Mustangs (7-2) 51, Fri., Nov. 6, Gerald J. Ford Stadium, Dallas. Next: vs Stanford, Sat., Nov. 14, Lane Stadium, Blacksburg
articles.text:
Virginia Tech Hokies 28, SMU Mustangs 51. Final score 51-28 from Dallas, and it stings in a real way. We are 6-3 and 3-3 in the ACC after a Friday night that got away early and never came all the way back. Entering the year with James Franklin, this was supposed to be a measuring-stick road trip. Instead Ford Stadium measured us and kept the ruler.

Jeffrey Overton Jr. was the bright spot. Thirteen carries for 123 yards and two touchdowns, including a 22-yard burst that made it 14-20 before the half and a 2-yard plunge in the fourth. Ethan Grunkemeyer went 28 of 38 for 291 yards, ran one in from a yard out, and found Que'Sean Brown from 3 late. Luke Reynolds caught six for 67. Noah Chambers led us with 11 tackles. Brennan Johnson picked one off for 22 yards. We put up 417 yards and 23 first downs. On another night that wins you a road game.

Not this night. Kevin Jennings carved us for 350 yards and four scores. Yamir Knight caught three of them. SMU racked up 569 yards and scored on drive after drive. We lost a fumble that flipped into a 46-yard Knight touchdown. Brendan Baird drilled kicks from 47, 26 and 50. We got blanked in the first quarter, blanked again in the third, and watched the Mustangs answer every punch.

The fourth quarter had some fight. Overton, then Brown, but Jalen Cooper's 50-yard score made it 51-28 and closed the book. Two turnovers. Too many empty possessions when the game was still in reach. That is a hard flight home.

Stanford comes to Lane Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Home cooking. Fix the ball security, stack a full four quarters, and remind everybody who we are when Blacksburg gets loud. Let's go.

Stanford comes to Lane Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. Home cooking. Fix the ball security, stack a full four quarters, and remind everybody who we are when Blacksburg gets loud. Let's go.

Fifty-one to twenty-eight. Gerald J. Ford Stadium on a clear Friday night, 32,566 of us packed into Dallas, and the Mustangs just hung a 51-28 final on Virginia Tech. Seven and two. Five and two in the ACC. Home fortress still untouched in league play. Write it down, grin, and play it back all weekend.

Kevin Jennings was dealing all night. Twenty-four of 32 for 350 yards and four touchdowns. Yamir Knight turned into a highlight reel: six grabs for 103 yards and three scores, including a 46-yard strike that made it 20-7 and later scores from 13 and 5. Brendan Baird was perfect on three field goals from 47, 26 and 50, plus all six extras. Fifteen points from the kicker's foot alone.

We scored on the first eight drives, per the AP wrap, and piled up 569 yards of offense with 219 on the ground. Alexander Kilgore led us with 10 tackles. Jimmy Wyrick snagged an interception. Marques White fell on a Virginia Tech fumble that set up Knight's long score. The Hokies got Jeffrey Overton Jr. for 123 yards and two scores, and Ethan Grunkemeyer threw for 291, but they never got the Ford Stadium crowd quiet for long.

Third quarter buried them: Raphael from 3, then Knight from 13, and suddenly it was 37-14. Knight again from 5 in the fourth. Cooper's 50-yarder after Virginia Tech scratched back to 28-44. That is how you send a Friday night crowd home happy in Dallas.

Wake Forest comes to Dallas on Saturday, Nov. 14, at noon ET. Same building. Same energy. The Mustangs are rolling, and November still belongs to us.

articles.title: Arizona vs TCU: Pooch Kick, Salgado-Medina Steal It 29-28
articles.matchup: Final: TCU Horned Frogs (4-5) 28, Arizona Wildcats (7-2) 29, Fri., Nov. 6, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson. Next: vs Utah, Sat., Nov. 14, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson
articles.text:
Arizona Wildcats 29, TCU Horned Frogs 28, and I do not have a voice left after Friday night at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Final score 29-28. Downtown Tucson spent the evening at Jácome Plaza for Tucson Greek Fest, a two-day party built on philoxenia, the Greek tradition of welcoming every guest. We welcomed TCU to town, too. Then, with 38 seconds left, we politely showed the Horned Frogs the door.

It did not look like a magic night for a while. Noah Fifita opened with a beauty, a 20-yard touchdown throw that Isaiah Mizell dove for, and Michael Salgado-Medina banged a 43-yarder for a 10-0 lead. Then the desert went dry. Late in the second quarter, deep in TCU territory, Hudson Hooper jumped a throw to the flat and ran 93 yards the other way. Down 14-10 at halftime. That one felt like grabbing a cholla barehanded.

Fifita kept swinging. He ran one in from 9 to retake the lead in the third, and Salgado-Medina's 23-yarder pulled us to 21-20 to open the fourth. But Jaden Craig bulled in from 2 for a 28-20 TCU lead, and the clock got loud. With 1:45 left, Fifita found Quincy Craig from 15 to make it 28-26. The two-point try died. My heart nearly joined it.

Then came the play this town will retell at every tailgate until spring. Ian French floated an onside pooch kick, Ed Small could not come up with it, and Zuri Watson pounced at the TCU 26. Four plays later Salgado-Medina drilled a 37-yarder. Three tries, three makes, 11 points from our kicker. Tyrese Boss intercepted Craig on the last TCU drive, and Tucson exploded.

Giovanni Richardson kept bailing us out all night: 11 catches for 171 yards, the long one going 46. Fifita threw for 313 and two scores. Taye Brown made 10 tackles. We are 7-2, 4-2 in the Big 12, and the AP says that is seven straight home wins, the longest run here since the 1993 and 1994 seasons.

Utah comes to Tucson on Saturday, Nov. 14, kickoff time still to be set, and the Big 12 race runs straight through our desert. I'll grab loukoumades from Papou's Cafe at Jácome Plaza on the way home. Bear Down, Tucson.

articles.title: TCU vs Arizona: Hooper's 93-Yard Return Not Enough, 28-29
articles.matchup: Final: TCU Horned Frogs (4-5) 28, Arizona Wildcats (7-2) 29, Fri., Nov. 6, Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson. Next: vs Kansas State, Sat., Nov. 14, Amon G. Carter Stadium, Fort Worth
articles.text:
TCU Horned Frogs 28, Arizona Wildcats 29. That 29-28 final from Casino Del Sol Stadium is going to ride around in my truck all week. We led Arizona 28-20 with 6:35 to play in Tucson on Friday night and still came home 4-5, 2-4 in the Big 12. Back in Fort Worth, Frog Fountain spent Friday afternoon hosting Frogchella 2.0, the First Gen Day party for TCU's first-generation students, with food, games and music. Campus spent the day honoring firsts. Our football team spent the night 38 seconds away from beating a ranked Big 12 team on the road.

Hudson Hooper was the best player on that field for long stretches. Twelve tackles, and with Arizona knocking on our door late in the second quarter, he jumped a throw to the flat and ran it back 93 yards for a touchdown. That flipped a 10-0 hole into a 14-10 halftime lead, and I nearly threw my hat into the rafters of my living room. Jaden Craig ducked a sack and scrambled 7 yards for our first score, hit Jordan Dwyer from 6 in the third quarter, and bulled in from 2 in the fourth. Craig finished 28 of 41 for 232 yards. Kari Ashley caught 14 balls for 95. Dwyer added nine grabs for 86.

Then the floor gave way. Arizona cut it to 28-26 with 1:45 left, the two-point try failed, and for a few seconds all of Frog Nation exhaled. Then Ian French floated an onside pooch kick, Ed Small could not come up with it, and Zuri Watson fell on the ball at our 26. Four plays later Michael Salgado-Medina hit from 37 with 38 seconds showing. Tyrese Boss intercepted Craig on our last try, and the desert went home happy.

The fix list writes itself. Kyle Lemmermann missed both of his field goal tries, and that is six points left in the cactus. We ran for 49 yards on 21 carries. Arizona piled up 441 yards to our 281, with Giovanni Richardson catching 11 balls for 171. Eight flags for 55 yards. I would love to blame Dallas for every one of those, and I will try, but the film is the film.

Kansas State comes to Amon G. Carter Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14, kickoff time still to be announced, and Utah follows a week later. Get home, get the run game fixed, and give Fort Worth a Saturday that ends with my hat in the air. Riff ram, Frogs.
